key_insight: Simplex-Constrained Sparse Bagging replaces uniform ensemble voting with a sparse, learned probability distribution over base models to improve calibration and compress the ensemble without sacrificing accuracy.
engineering_relevance: It offers a model-agnostic post-training compression method that can cut inference cost and improve reliability for deployed bagging systems such as Random Forests and Bagged Neural Networks.
method: Optimize ensemble weights on the probability simplex using OOB loss
Use a concave quadratic penalty to induce sparsity because L1 cannot prune on the simplex
Prune low-weight estimators to form a compressed calibrated ensemble
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 96% ensemble compression, linear inference speedups, lower Expected Calibration Error, and preserved or improved generalization accuracy.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of OOB estimates and the nonconvex optimization may be sensitive to tuning and convergence behavior.
paper_title: Simplex-Constrained Sparse Bagging: Transitioning from Uniform Priors to Sparse Posteriors in Ensemble Learning
